behavioral_notes.observation: import_module() base64-decodes module_file into a BytesIO and calls IrModule._import_zipfile(fp, force, with_demo), then redirects the client to /odoo. _import_zipfile FIRST gates on self.env.is_admin() (raises AccessError 'Only administrators can install data modules'), rejects non-zip input (zipfile.is_zipfile) and any entry exceeding MAX_FILE_SIZE=100MB. It opens the archive into a file_open_temporary_directory, finds each top-level dir holding a MANIFEST_NAMES file, parses each manifest via Manifest._from_path, topological_sort's the modules by their 'depends', and extracts only the data/static/i18n files of each. It then calls self.sudo()._import_module(mod_name, path, force, with_demo) per module in dependency order, wrapping any failure in a UserError carrying the full traceback. None of this zip-unpacking / dependency-ordering / admin-gating is visible in metadata.

Registers a module into the live database WITHOUT it being on the addons-path at boot. It parses the manifest (Manifest._from_path), builds ir.module.module values via get_values_from_terp, then either writes an existing ir.module.module to state='installed' (mode='update', or 'init' if force) or CREATES a new record with imported=True, state='installed' (mode='init'). Unmet 'depends' are button_immediate_install'd first (raising UserError on truly unknown deps); web_studio-authored modules are refused unless Studio is installed (_is_studio_custom scans XML records for a studio context key). It refuses 'industries' data modules differently (module_type='industries' when context data_module). This bypasses the normal -i/-u CLI install flow, which metadata cannot reveal.

behavioral_notes.element: _import_module: loading data files via convert_file + static assets + i18n as ir.attachment
behavioral_notes.observation: For each kind in ['data','init_xml'(+'demo' if with_demo)], for every manifest-declared filename ending in .xml/.csv/.sql it calls odoo.tools.convert_file(env, module, filename, idref, mode, noupdate, pathname) to load the records into the DB (csv under init_xml is forced noupdate). It then walks <module>/static and stores EVERY static file as a base64 ir.attachment with url '/<module>/...' and res_model='ir.ui.view' (public) so JS/CSS/images are served from the DB, not disk; .po files under i18n are stored as binary ir.attachment for webclient translation; manifest 'assets' bundles become ir.asset rows (glob wildcards rejected). Each gets an ir.model.data row for clean uninstall. This DB-as-filesystem behaviour for imported modules is pure code semantics.

A type='http', auth='none', POST, csrf=False, save_session=False endpoint that authenticates inline from posted login/password (request.session.authenticate), and ONLY if request.env.uid is set (None under MFA) AND request.env.user._is_admin() does it call ir.module.module._import_zipfile(mod_file, force=force=='1') and return its message. Otherwise it raises AccessError; any exception is returned as an HTTP 500 with the error text. This is the scriptable/CI counterpart to the UI wizard (odoo-bin module-upload), letting an admin push a .zip module over HTTP. The force='1' query param maps to _import_module mode='init' (re-init noupdate records); without it mode='update'.

behavioral_notes.element: module_uninstall + button_upgrade overrides (imported modules are special-cased)
behavioral_notes.observation: module_uninstall() captures imported modules BEFORE super() (the 'imported' column may vanish mid-uninstall) and unlink()s them entirely after uninstall - because an imported module cannot be reinstalled (its data files are gone from disk), so the record is deleted rather than left 'uninstalled'. button_upgrade() reverts any imported module pushed to 'to upgrade' back to 'installed', since imported modules cannot be upgraded through the standard flow. _get_modules_to_load_domain excludes imported modules from the regular boot load. These lifecycle divergences are invisible to metadata.

Two small JS files, no OWL component of its own and no QWeb template. base_import_list_view.js spreads @web/views/list/list_view, swaps in ImportModuleListRenderer, and registry.category('views').add('ir_module_module_tree_view', ...) so the Apps/Industries module list renders with a custom renderer (driving the 'more_info' action that opens a module form). Behaviour lives entirely in static assets, not Python views.

runtime.note: base.import.module is a transient (wizard) model (ephemeral rows). The persistent footprint is on ir.module.module (imported=True rows) which accrue only when an admin actually imports a module. Not run live in this pass.

classification.rationale: base_import_module is runtime module-deployment tooling - firm IT infrastructure with no business object of its own. Its only persistent additions are bookkeeping on ir.module.module (imported, module_type); base.import.module is a transient upload wizard. It creates no value-stream output of any chain/shop/network; it acts ON the platform itself, registering uploaded code/data modules into the live database and managing their install/upgrade/uninstall lifecycle. This is a Porter support activity (Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'): auto_install=true, depends only on web, and its substance is application deployment / change management - taking a packaged module and provisioning it into the running platform. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits squarely (deploy/maintain application solutions, manage change/release of application components). 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was considered (runtime import underpins onboarding industry capabilities) but rejected: this is a concrete running deployment utility, not a governance/portfolio capability - its work is IT application deployment, i.e. 8.0. Mirrors the sibling base_import and web classifications (support / 8.0): framework plumbing whose substance is IT delivery, not a business activity.
